claims.text: Fl!vio Bolsonaro won the first round of Brazil's presidential election, beating incumbent President Luiz In!cio Lula da Silva, but failed to secure over 50% of the vote required for an outright victory.
A runoff election between Fl!vio Bolsonaro and Luiz In!cio Lula da Silva is scheduled for October 25.
With 98.81% of the votes counted in the first round, Fl!vio Bolsonaro held 47.24% of the vote compared to Lula's 44.91%.
Fl!vio Bolsonaro is the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year prison sentence for masterminding a failed coup attempt.
Former president Jair Bolsonaro's wife, Michelle, was elected to the Senate.
After casting his ballot, Lula warned that the choice in the election was between democracy and 'barbarism'.
The president of Brazil's supreme electoral court stated that no evidence of international interference was found in the election.
With more than 99% of ballots processed in Brazil's election, Fl!vio Bolsonaro had received 47.2% of the vote and Lula da Silva had received 45%.
'Brazil needs change,' Fl!vio Bolsonaro said as he cast his vote on Sunday.
In September, it was revealed that Fl!vio Bolsonaro is under investigation for alleged corruption, money laundering, and tax evasion tied to financing a biopic about his father.
The winner of the Brazilian presidential runoff election will take power on January 5, 2027.
No presidential candidate has won the presidency of Brazil since democracy returned in the 1980s without winning in the state of Minas Gerais.
Nearly 159 million eligible voters in Brazil were tasked with electing 27 state governors, federal lower house representatives, and 54 senators alongside the president.
Early election results showed significant right-wing gains across Brazil's Congress, particularly in the Senate.
Six Russian drones struck an Indian pharmaceutical plant operated by Kusum Group in Sumy, Ukraine, killing an engineer and destroying the main facility.
Kusum Healthcare projected that total damage from the drone attack on its Sumy facility will exceed $50 million.
Ukraine and Germany signed a $1.5 billion (1.3 billion euro) agreement for weapons and energy support during German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's visit to Kyiv.
The $1.5 billion deal between Ukraine and Germany includes approximately 1 billion euros for weapons and 350 million euros for Ukraine's energy sector.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called Russian strikes on Ukrainian civilians 'war crimes that are being committed daily here'.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that Ukraine is ready to engage in US-backed trilateral technical talks with Russia by the end of October.
Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar stated in New Delhi that India is stepping up efforts to mediate in the Ukraine conflict.
A Russian drone struck Kyiv's Northern Bridge over the Dnipro River, injuring two people on the fourth consecutive day of strikes on the city's bridges.
Germany became Ukraine's largest military aid provider after Friedrich Merz took office in May 2025.
Russia's foreign ministry warned foreign nationals and diplomatic personnel against remaining in or traveling to Ukraine.
EU Ambassador Katar!na Mathernov! posted on social media: 'Threatening us will not stop Europe's support for Ukraine. It only reminds us why that support matters!'
Rashad al-Alimi, head of Yemen's presidential council, declared the start of a military operation to retake all territory held by the Houthis.
Houthi forces severed a vital supply road connecting Taiz to Aden after taking control of the al-Safiya area and a local police station.
Recent fighting in and around Yemen's Taiz province killed over 70 people in 24 hours, including 34 government troops and 39 Houthi fighters.
Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed the group launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco facilities in Riyadh and Khurais.
The Yemeni government announced an offensive against Houthi forces as Iran stated its readiness to defend itself against potential US attacks.
'We will defeat and crush anyone who enters the city of Taiz,' declared Taiz resident Zakaria Al-Dhubhani.
A Houthi offensive last month allowed the group to take control of Yemen's Red Sea coastline and the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
The Pentagon confirmed that all US B-1 bomber aircraft deployed to RAF Fairford in the United Kingdom have been redeployed back to their home bases in the United States.
Police were called to RAF Fairford after a local farmer reported suspicious activity involving several vans and a group of men.
Counter-terrorism officers found petrol inside vans near RAF Fairford, but no explosive materials were discovered.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated that Britain had 'strong indications' pointing to Iranian involvement in a plot targeting RAF Fairford.
Iran rejected accusations connecting Tehran to the alleged airbase plot and summoned the British ambassador in Tehran.
British police arrested a 25-year-old UK-Iranian dual national in London on suspicion of plotting an attack on RAF Fairford.
The US and Israel have been engaged in an active war against Iran that began on February 28.
UK Defense Secretary Wes Streeting stated that Iran was likely responsible for the thwarted plot at RAF Fairford, though the UK had not yet made a formal attribution.
A US naval deployment heading to the Middle East featuring the USS Theodore Roosevelt and USS Malkin Island carries over 7,000 sailors and 2,000 Marines.
Leaders from Egypt, Eritrea, Somalia, and Sudan issued a joint declaration in Egypt calling for peaceful political solutions to regional conflicts.
Ethiopian government forces retook Mekelle after the Tigray People's Liberation Front announced a temporary withdrawal from the city.
Former Tigray interim leader Abraham Belay stated that Ethiopia is preparing a temporary administration for Tigray and plans to hold regional elections within months.
The TPLF formed an alliance with six other armed groups, including the Amhara Fano militia, aimed at removing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed from power.
Ethiopia and Eritrea severed diplomatic ties after Ethiopia accused Eritrea of supporting the new rebel coalition.
Ethiopian federal troops began patrolling Mekelle and securing key government institutions as city communications were restored.
TPLF leader Debretsion Gebremichael stated: 'We operate under a strategy to strike the enemy wherever we choose.'
French Education Minister !douard Geffray announced that between 400 and 500 high schools will be totally or partially closed on Monday due to safety concerns from student protests.
According to the French education minister, 24 schools have been burned or ransacked since student demonstrations began in mid-September.
Over 5,000 people have been arrested in France during the past week of student protests, with 85 percent being minors.
Education Minister !douard Geffray reported that 78 education staff members have been injured during the school unrest.
Police in La Ciotat detained a 16-year-old after a 59-year-old teacher was struck and doused with gasoline during a high school protest.
More than 600 police officers have been injured across France during the student protest movement.
The high school protest movement originated at a Paris school on September 17 over concerns regarding teacher absences, long school days, and poor building conditions.
French Prime Minister S!bastien Lecornu asked local authorities to prioritize filling long-term teaching gaps and scheduled a regional meeting on school infrastructure.
